Tax filing deadline

A national tax site lets 30 million people file online. Most wait until deadline day, and traffic climbs all evening to a final-hour rush. People upload forms, check what they owe and pay. A mistake in a payment or a leak of tax data is a national story. Practise this hard system design problem for free, with no sign-up.

The brief

A national tax site lets 30 million people file online. Most wait until deadline day, and traffic climbs all evening to a final-hour rush. People upload forms, check what they owe and pay. A mistake in a payment or a leak of tax data is a national story.

Think of a national tax filing site.

Users, scale and requirements

Who uses it
30 million filers over the season (approx.)
Audience in plain numbers
30,000,000 users or devices
Normal peak
≈ 8,000 requests per second
Request mix
Read: 49%; Write: 22%; Sign-in: 15%; Notification: 1%; Upload: 6%; Payment: 4%; Report: 3%
Speed for 99 of 100 requests
Read: ≈ 700 ms; Write: ≈ 700 ms; Sign-in: ≈ 1,000 ms; Upload: ≈ 4,000 ms; Payment: ≈ 3,000 ms; Report: ≈ 10,000 ms
Successful requests
99.9%
Data safety
No acknowledged write may be lost.
Monthly budget
≈ $260,000
Data at rest
≈ 80 TB
Where users are
North America: 100%
Home region
North America
Waiting deadlines
Read: 900 seconds; Write: 3,600 seconds; Sign-in: 900 seconds; Notification: 900 seconds; Upload: 3,600 seconds; Payment: 3,600 seconds; Report: 3,600 seconds
Minimum retained history
2,555 days on authoritative stores
Fresh reads
People must see their own changes. At most 0.1% of reads may be stale in the model.
Personal reads
80% of reads are private; a shared public copy cannot answer them.
Required proofs
Audit trail; Managed encryption keys; Personal data isolated; Tested backups; Signed-in access; Retention rules

≈ marks an approximation, just as in the game. Waiting deadlines measure the age of queued work and are separate from interactive response time.

  • The deadline-day curve climbs to 1.0 at 23:30, and an extra rush on top triples the last stretch.
  • A "write" is saving a draft or submitting a return.
  • Scored data retention: at least 2555 days on active authoritative stores. Copies used only for search or reports can be rebuilt. Local device history and rollup policies still require the separate protocol check.
  • Notification speed measures provider acceptance. Device receipt is outside this traffic model; check expiry, provider outcome and retries in the correctness trace before claiming delivery guarantees.

Questions that shape the design

When is the rush?

The deadline is 23:30 on the last day. Traffic builds from the afternoon and peaks in the final hour at about three times the already high evening level.

Can a payment be taken twice?

Never. Every payment must happen exactly once, even when the person presses pay again or their phone retries.

What if the identity-check provider rate-limits us?

It happens in the rush. Sign-ins that cannot be verified right now must wait, not fail forever.

What does an auditor ask for?

Proof of an audit trail, encryption, isolated personal data, backups, signed-in access and retention for years.

The traffic day

Traffic builds toward a deadline. The clock covers 00:00 to 24:00 in the home region. Events add pressure on top of that normal traffic.

  1. 15:00 · Compliance audit

    An auditor checks your design: who did what, encryption keys, personal data, backups and consent.

  2. 18:00 · Deadline surge

    Tax day, enrollment close or a sign-up deadline. Traffic climbs for hours until the cut-off.

    Traffic reaches 3 times the scheduled load; rises over 14,400 seconds, holds for 3,600 seconds and eases over 600 seconds.

  3. 22:00 · Provider rate limit

    An outside service lowers its configured request quota and answers 'too many requests' above the reduced limit.

    Provider capacity falls to 50% of its configured quota. Duration: ≈ 3,600 seconds.

What a strong design has to handle

  • The load arrives slowly and then all at once. What element adds servers as the day builds, and why will it still be late?
  • Issue durable filing receipts and reconcile payments independently of deadline retries.
  • Autoscaling takes a few minutes to add servers, so the design pre-sizes to 20 and scales on a climb that starts hours early. A sudden minute-long jump would still hurt.
  • The queue lets the site accept a return in a moment and finish processing it later; the person sees "received" and gets a confirmation after.

Make a prediction, run a full traffic day, then compare the result. The in-game editorial opens after a finished day and includes measured reference designs.

Concepts to practise

  • Waiting instead of breaking
  • Adding servers, and why it is late
  • Proof built in
